title: Seafin homepage: four directions, rendered
question: Each card is a real first screen built from the same content. Keep the Nameplate, take a new one, or re-roll.

options.label: The Storefront Window
options.lineage: gold-leaf sign painting on Main Street shop windows
options.thesis: Seafin as a founder-run shop on Main Street, its offer painted in gold leaf on the window.
options.viewport: Gold-leaf headline on black glass, the offer and founder below, and the request form on an 'Inquire within' card hanging in the window.
options.risk: Gold leaf can tip into saloon or barbershop nostalgia; the lettering has to stay crisp and the script used once.

raised.raise: One window, one pane: every section below continues on the same glass and frame, never a second sign.
One law for the layout: everything aligns to the window's gold pinstripe border.

options.label: The Work Order
options.thesis: The page is the work order a contractor fills in: scope, technician, terms, and the customer box you fill.
options.viewport: Headline handwritten in the Description of work box, technician and terms below, and the Customer box as the request form with a rubber-stamp button.
options.risk: Handwriting reads as cute if overdone, and the canary sheet is loud by design.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: Seafin as a stack of one-bit cards you click through.
options.viewport: A card window carrying the offer, and a request card with real fields and a 'Book a free call' button.
options.case: Clear and memorable, and nostalgic for owners who grew up on early Macs; younger buyers may read it as a gimmick.
options.risk: Retro novelty if the type gets small.

options.label: The Equipment Nameplate
options.thesis: AI as equipment you own: plated, installed where you choose, serviced by the person who built it.
options.viewport: Cobalt plate with the headline, a field table, 'Property of: your business', and the request form in the plate's service band.
options.risk: The review asked for 8 fixes: a bigger 'your business', one amber button, flatter screws, one grid.

options.label: Orizuru Crane
options.thesis: One red sheet folded step by step into a crane.
options.viewport: A single red sheet showing its folds.
options.case: Beautiful, but owners of clinics and law firms don't see themselves in origami, and the folds hide the offer.
options.kept: One continuous sheet: nothing becomes a second object.
options.risk: Art piece, not a business page.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.thesis: One frozen collision with tracks curving through detector rings.
options.viewport: A dark ring diagram with glowing tracks.
options.case: Near-black with neon is the AI-site cliché, and physics imagery says nothing to a small-business owner.
options.kept: One compositional law the whole page obeys.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What small AI consultancies ship, executed well.
canonCard.viewport: Outcome headline and a book-a-call button beside the founder's photo, three service cards, a process strip, FAQ.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other AI consultancy, by design.
